evidence: src/domain/order-state.ts: FULFILMENT_FLOW, CANCELLABLE, nextState and isCancellable are the only definitions of order states and transitions; src/domain/order.ts Order.advanceTo and Order.cancel call nextState and isCancellable.
src/domain/product.ts: Product.available and Product.canReserve hold the stock-availability rule; Product.reserve uses canReserve.

src/domain/stock-reservation.ts: reserveStock checks with product.canReserve(quantity) before changing anything, then calls productFor(...).reserve(quantity); releaseStock calls Product.release, so stock changes only go through Product.
src/domain/order-line.ts: the OrderLine constructor is the only place the positive-integer quantity check is made.
src/domain/order-repository.ts and src/domain/product-repository.ts: the interfaces are written in terms of Order, OrderState and Product.

Minor: src/domain/stock-reservation.ts reserveStock and src/domain/product.ts Product.reserve both build DomainError('insufficient_stock', 'Insufficient stock for product ...') with the same wording. This duplicates the message, not the rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All eight files serve one concern: orders, their lines, product stock and reserving stock for orders. They use the DomainError/DomainErrorCode abstraction consistently. Order states and their transitions are defined only in order-state.ts (FULFILMENT_FLOW, CANCELLABLE, nextState, isCancellable), and Order.advanceTo and Order.cancel call into it. The line-quantity check lives only in the OrderLine constructor. The stock rules (available = onHand - reserved, canReserve) live only in Product. stock-reservation.ts builds on Product instead of going around it: reserveStock checks every line with product.canReserve first and then changes stock only through product.reserve, so all lines are reserved or none. The repository interfaces are written in terms of the module's own types. Minor issue: reserveStock builds the same insufficient_stock DomainError, with the same wording, as Product.reserve. The check itself is still only in Product.canReserve, so this is duplicated wording, not a duplicated rule. Minor inconsistency: releaseStock skips products it can't find while reserveStock raises not_found, which is reasonable for a release step. Neither reaches the fail threshold.
